clue.text: Father sat on spike to entertain posh people

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to hold them within, so the posh letter goes inside

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father
to spike a drink is to lace it
U is the old label for upper-class, posh usage

explanation.surface: A father perched on a spike while hosting upper-class guests.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'sat on' means placed above; U as posh is the old 'U and non-U' class label.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the populace is the common people of a place as a whole.

clue.text: One's served beefcake

definitions.meaning: something served up at a meal
slang for an attractive person, as beefcake is a handsome muscular man

explanation.surface: Someone is presented with a hunk of beef on a plate.
explanation.definitionFit: A plate of food is served, and a good-looking person is informally a real looker or hunk.

clue.text: Where neither is more likely to lift alcoholic drink

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting raises the word so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunkard
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: A situation finely balanced as to whether someone will raise their glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lift' only works in a down clue, where reading upward reverses the word; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A coin flip is an even chance, so the phrase names a situation with equal odds either way.

clue.text: See 20
Stir miso soup faster

indicators.note: stirring the soup mixes its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to stir miso soup more quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faster' looks like an adverb about stirring; it is the musical direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian musical direction meaning 'more movement', i.e. play more quickly.

clue.text: Accidental breakdown ultimately contained by body of soldiers, having come to a halt

indicators.note: contained by means that letter sits inside the military body

parts.note: a unit is a body of soldiers

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word breakdown

parts.note: something that has come to a halt has ended

explanation.surface: An accidental breakdown stopped a troop of soldiers in its tracks.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something accidental was not meant or planned.

clue.text: Meat finally picked from bone in Spanish food

indicators.note: picked from means that letter is plucked out of the bone

parts.note: the patella is the kneecap bone

indicators.note: finally selects the closing letter of the word Meat

explanation.surface: The last scrap of meat is picked off a bone in a Spanish dish.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing T from PATELLA, the kneecap, leaves the dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the rice dish from Valencia is a classic Spanish food.

clue.text: Piece turned to compress two gases in forming diamond

indicators.note: to compress is to squeeze something in, so the gases go inside
turned means the chess word is read backwards

parts.note: a rook is a chess piece
O and H are the symbols for oxygen and hydrogen
taken as written

explanation.surface: A chess piece rotated to squeeze gases while forming a diamond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two gases' are chemical symbols, oxygen and hydrogen; the reversed chess word holds them after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Name: the famous Indian gem set in the British Crown Jewels is a diamond.

clue.text: One occupying island with name Odysseus, perhaps?

indicators.note: occupying means the numeral sits inside the island

parts.note: Iona is an island in the Inner Hebrides
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone settling on an island with a name, as Odysseus might have.
explanation.walkthrough: Odysseus was king of Ithaca, one of the Ionian Islands; the '?' flags him as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Odysseus came from Ithaca in the Greek sea west of the mainland, so he was a native of those islands.

clue.text: One's saddled with Spooner's fish in the outback?

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the two words trade first letters

parts.note: the bush is the Australian outback
the pike is a predatory freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Someone is stuck with a fish from the Australian bush, Spooner-style.
explanation.walkthrough: BUSH PIKE swaps its initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedal bicycles carry a saddle, so the definition describes one by that seat.

clue.text: How well a gala might have gone?

definitions.text: How well a gala might have gone?

parts.words: How well a gala might have gone?
parts.note: a swimming gala is a competitive swimming event, and an event that went very well went smoothly

explanation.surface: Wondering how a festive event went.
explanation.walkthrough: A swimming gala is a British school or club swimming competition.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: things going smoothly and successfully, with a pun on the swimming at a gala.

clue.text: See 17
Cook creating delicious and enticing starters in a hundred steps

indicators.note: to cook something up is to concoct it, so these letters are rearranged
starters means the opening letters of delicious and enticing

explanation.surface: A chef creating tasty appetising first courses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' rearranges CREATING into CENTIGRA; 'starters' gives D and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal split: centi means hundred and grade means step, describing a scale of a hundred degrees.

clue.text: Female boxing star in US city

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the girl wraps around the star

parts.note: a lass is a girl or young woman
Vega is the brightest star in Lyra

explanation.surface: A female boxer who is a star in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing' is not the sport but enclosing; the star is Vega, in Lyra.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Nevada gambling resort is a US city.

clue.text: See 23
Clip of Irish islands showing boat

parts.note: to clip is to trim
the Aran Islands lie off Galway in Ireland

explanation.surface: A film clip of Irish islands featuring a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a sailing vessel with three hulls is a type of boat.

clue.text: Wicked work by council leader repeatedly questioning technique that's in force?

indicators.note: repeatedly signals that the council letter and work come twice

parts.note: wicked is slang for good, and in its plain sense it means bad, which the repeat uses

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word council

parts.note: the council's leader again, taken a second time as the clue says
OP is short for opus, a work
in its plain sense wicked means evil or bad, the second of its two opposite senses
the council's leader again, its first letter taken a second time as the clue says

explanation.surface: A wicked council head repeatedly interrogating someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wicked' works twice in opposite senses (slang praise, then plain evil), and 'repeatedly' says C and OP come twice. The force is the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a police interrogation method pairing a friendly officer with a hostile one.

clue.text: At least 51 also across the terrain

parts.note: over L, i.e. more than fifty in Roman numerals
and means also

explanation.surface: At least 51 people also crossed the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: L is Roman 50, so 'over L' means above fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: travel by land rather than sea or air goes across the ground.

clue.text: Force unit to seal off West Crawley, perhaps?

indicators.note: to seal something off is to enclose it, so the unit surrounds the compass letter

parts.note: the newton is the SI unit of force

explanation.surface: Police sealing off the west of Crawley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Force' suggests police but is physics. Crawley is a postwar planned town in West Sussex.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Crawley was one of Britain's postwar planned settlements.

clue.text: The idiot in life reacted and I adapted

indicators.note: adapted means altered, so all these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a nit is a fool

explanation.surface: A fool reacted in life, and I adapted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The' is the definition: grammatically it is this kind of word.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: in grammar the word 'the' is the English specific determiner.

clue.text: Maximum amount of wax, perhaps, for carpeting?

definitions.meaning: an ear full of wax is as much as it holds
a carpeting is a severe telling-off

explanation.surface: Asking how much floor wax goes on a carpet.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy scolding is a stream of words poured on the listener, as is a carpeting.

clue.text: A mammalian plague

definitions.meaning: a mammal, here a black-and-white burrowing animal

explanation.surface: A disease spread among mammals.
explanation.definitionFit: A burrowing mammal, and as a verb to pester someone persistently.

clue.text: Begin to understand financial plan

parts.note: to bud is to begin growing
to get something is to understand it

explanation.surface: Starting to grasp a financial plan.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an estimate of income and spending is a financial plan.

clue.text: Local favourite criticised, wearing unimaginative strip

indicators.note: wearing means the criticised word is clothed by the next pieces

parts.note: dry means dull or unimaginative
Peanuts is the Charlie Brown comic strip
to roast is to criticise harshly

explanation.surface: A popular local figure is criticised for wearing a dull kit.
explanation.walkthrough: A local is a British regular pub; 'strip' is a comic strip, not team kit.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: salted nuts are a favourite bar snack at a British pub.

clue.text: See 26
See 10
Plain fish to catch way back

indicators.note: to catch is to hold within, so the fish surrounds it

parts.note: tuna is a fish

indicators.note: back means the road abbreviation reads in reverse

parts.note: RD is short for road, a way

explanation.surface: Fishing simply, and heading back home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' looks like an adjective (simply) but is the noun, a flat expanse.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the treeless Arctic expanse is a vast plain.

clue.text: Ground crew and leader join party that should bring the house down

definitions.text: that should bring the house down

indicators.note: ground means crushed, so the letters are broken up and reformed

parts.note: a king is a leader
a ball is a formal dance party

explanation.surface: Ground staff and their boss throw a party meant to be a smash hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bring the house down' means a rousing success, but here literally demolition.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal: a heavy swinging weight used in demolition knocks buildings to the ground.
